Soul Cakes

Served at: All Hallows' Eve (Halloween)

Makes about 12 cakesPrep 20 minCook 15 min

Soul Cakes are small, spiced round cakes traditionally made and given out during All Hallows' Eve, or Halloween. They are part of an old custom where children and the poor would go 'souling,' singing and receiving these cakes in return for prayers for the dead. These cakes symbolize the souls of the departed and are a delicious way to connect with the festival's history.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) currants or raisins
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) milk
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) brandy or apple juice (optional)
  • 1 egg yolk (for glaze)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, baking powder, and salt.
  3. Cut in the cold butter using a pastry cutter or your fingers until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
  4. Stir in the currants or raisins.
  5. In a separate bowl, beat the egg with milk, vanilla extract, and brandy or apple juice if using.
  6. Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until just combined to form a dough.
  7. Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and gently knead it a few times to bring it together.
  8. Roll the dough out to about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thickness and cut into rounds using a cookie cutter or glass.
  9. Place the rounds on the prepared baking sheet.
  10. Brush the tops with egg yolk for a shiny finish.
  11. Bake for 12-15 minutes or until golden brown.
  12. Allow to cool on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, soak the currants or raisins in warm brandy or apple juice for 30 minutes before adding to the dough.
  • You can add a pinch of ground allspice or ginger for extra warmth.
  • Serve soul cakes with a cup of tea or cider for a traditional Halloween treat.
